item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Tuesday, 20 October 2026
item.description:
Stargrace pulled in 4.5 million WoW gold on pets, recipes, transmog, and crafting, while reshuffling auction alts ahead of WoW:Forever.

Azuriel says Valheim’s Ashlands wasn’t as brutal as advertised, then unloads on Fader as a tedious boss slog and outdated guides as their own menace.

Bhagpuss wrestles with Steam Next Fest’s messy tagging to pick demos, sticking mostly to familiar territory like MMORPGs, point-and-clicks, and strategy.

Emily recounts a vivid Halo-flavored dream of fleeing Jiralhanae, with Tartarus shout-outs and some very personal Brute-related grievances.

Marc breaks down how Slap Fight mixes Xevious-style shooting with Gradius upgrades and secret-hunting that subtly teaches the best weapons for each stretch.

Ellie finally digs into New Super Lucky’s Tale, chasing that old-school Spyro and Crash collectathon magic after Lil Gator Game rekindled the craving.

Wilhelm is all-in on Over the Hill, praising Funselektor’s stylized off-road driving, obsessive vehicle physics, and a weekend-devouring Steam launch.

Joel’s weeknotes bounce from card magic and a possibly dying SSD to gifted copies of Outer Wilds, fountain pens, books, and everyday life stuff.

Warner says a Tushy Spa bidet turned out to be a genuinely welcome household upgrade, installed by his handier son-in-law.

Syp scores a $5 second-gen iPod Shuffle at a thrift store and gets a charming little retro win, battery anxiety and weird iTunes autofill included.

Roger tracks a media-player playback glitch to a dying Zidoo remote, then does the homework to find a backward-compatible replacement.

Bruce Schneier flags a leaked Cellebrite document describing Advanced Unlocks, a possible new iPhone radio-based AFU zero-day with roughly 8-meter range.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Monday, 19 October 2026
item.description:
Frostilyte digs into Prison of Husks, a FromSoft-style demo whose gear-based progression and hidden equipment made its boss fights click.

Kimimi gushes over Baldur’s Gate III as a deeply reactive RPG whose tactical freedom and Astarion-fueled emotional pull still hit hard.

Margot talks herself into a Retroid Pocket Duo, chasing OLED dual-screen bliss for DS and 3DS emulation without going full handheld overkill.

Wilhelm rounds up a late Fantasy Critic shakeup, with Valor Mortis, Castlevania: Belmont’s Curse, and Planet Zoo 2 nudging the standings.

Anarchae’s weekly digest checks in on new-job nerves, disappointing library mysteries, reality TV, Raptors anticipation, and Fate/GO event progress.

Tan’s fortnightly digest bounces from Nier: Automata and Terranigma to record-player tinkering, teaching stress, and half-term relief.

Cristian calls it on The100Pics, bowing out of the photo event with a short, clean note of burnout.

Tobold argues disruptive protests target governments more effectively than school shootings, framing both as symptoms of young people’s desperation.

Ramen Junkie speedruns gripes about Epic’s Linux launcher, Character AI’s collapse, and Microsoft 365 storage cuts with appropriately cranky energy.

Scopique likes how Markdown can look in Obsidian, but hates how writing in raw syntax flips TTRPG prep from prose brain to coding brain.

Dave Winer ties his Markdown-web gripes to Chrome’s power, then pivots to a blunt complaint about US healthcare still running on phone tag.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Sunday, 18 October 2026
item.description:
Tipa dives into Enshrouded’s poisonous, boss-timed survival-crafting loop and sizes up its shared-world quirks against Valheim, Dune: Awakening, and Guild Wars 2.

Sey rounds up Galaxies Autumn Showcase standouts like Lelu, Kloa, MR. RECORDS, and Gravity Circuit 2 with plenty of wishlist energy.

Bhagpuss gets unexpectedly chills-over-spine invested in Neverness To Everness after Akane’s band-focused trailer turns his own character into the onstage drummer.

Shintar recounts leveling through WoW: Midnight on a ground mount only, finding extra immersion, fewer autopilot slipups, and more friction for mining.

Wes spotlights the newly uncovered F-Zero GX cheat codes, plus a broader roundup touching emulation hardware and translation work worth keeping an eye on.

The Chronicler previews SPIEL Essen 2026’s wargame side, with The Great Escape, Battle Commander, and a reminder that conflict games keep carving out space there.

Kelly reflects on friendship as a habit that needs tending, and how easy isolation makes it to let even meaningful connections drift.

Roger surveys his current TV habits, from Crystal Lake to Celebrity Traitors, with a nice side glance at why prestige television often leaves him cold.

Warner puts Sunday Morning Reading on a brief hiatus while enjoying Halloween-season grandkid time, with plans to return next week.

Wilhelm grumbles through modern streaming discovery, with Roku search, AMC+, BritBox, Prime Video, and the misery of watching old shows on FAST channels.

Juhis kicks off Djangonaut Space with onboarding, community events, first contributions, and the kind of open-source enthusiasm that makes mentorship programs feel genuinely inviting.

Tim Bray checks back in on X and comes away unconvinced, arguing the platform still feels algorithmically warped, propagandistic, and deeply joyless.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Saturday, 17 October 2026
item.description:
Stargrace is back on World of Warcraft, pushing story and Engineering progress while mulling ATT setup and hoping to finally find a social guild.

Aywren digs into her FFXIV alt chaos, juggling identities on a highly progressed character slot after finally settling her main on Amon.

John loves Maple Blade’s adorable, tactical ghost-bopping loop, even if the big complaint is simply that this lovely roguelike ends too soon.

Shintar reassesses SWTOR’s Legacy of the Sith as a whole, arguing the once-thin expansion filled out over time with lots of story and MMO content.

Luna finds Bloomtown underwhelming and barely horror, while Slay the Princess is landing the weird, choice-driven psychological dread much better.

Margot says Woodo’s cozy wooden diorama puzzles and textures are lovely, though the narration sometimes clashes with actually focusing on placement.

Pixel One is enjoying Aion 2’s classes and world, but says its Black character options lag badly behind Guild Wars 2’s standard.

Wilhelm notes Enshrouded’s 1.0 launch is pulling off a real second debut, with a player spike, full map access, and the new Cinder’s Cradle biome.

Anarchae turns a Mastodon outage into a diary-like check-in about DOS2 posting, shift planning, and the oddly offline rhythm of a regular evening.

Heartless is absolutely buzzing that the Milwaukee Brewers swept the Dodgers and are headed to the World Series.

Jimmy points readers to a new Analog Antiquarian entry, this time an Opus piece on The Taming of the Shrew.

Scopique melts a Star Citizen Ironclad Assault, grabs a Constellation Mk V, and weighs the RSI Galaxy around cargo, industry, and medical gameplay.

item.title: The Daily Blogroll — Friday, 16 October 2026
item.description:
Syp finally grabs RimWorld Odyssey and is already enjoying grasslands, fishing, flooding, and wind power as fresh puzzle pieces for his colony.

Azuriel weighs Tim Cain’s disappearing RPG features against modern budgets, arguing Bloodlines-style depth is great until production costs and sales realities bite.

Kimimi revisits Neverwinter Nights 2 and immediately runs into clunky foster-dad writing, flat stakes, and an opening that kills any sense of home.

David’s Battle Brothers raid the Gates of Power for mana crystals, dodge manticores and deadly dwarf halls, and keep their heads attached.

Wilhelm checks in on the WoW Forever beta, liking the old-school hunter grind and striking new lighting more than those weird HD human models.

Tobold says Transport Fever 3 gets fun once you stop fixing everything and triage city growth, supplies, and passenger lines instead.

Joel takes stock of a comfortable routine of work, games, church, and snacks, while admitting fitness, mess, and comfort-zone habits may need a shakeup.

Ramen Junkie says Studio Series 86 Prowl is a really nice G1 update held back by cartoon deco and a loose, aging waist joint.

Bruce Schneier flags poisoned open-weight AI models as a supply-chain nightmare: cheap to hide, hard to detect, and capable of credential theft on cue.

Dave Winer ships another Atlantis tweak for Markdown files, then unloads on Google for flagging an old Scripting archive while linkrot does real damage.

Cristian floats canceling Claude for Grok, basically tossing the question out to readers without much else to go on yet.

Axxuy likes pocket notebooks, but calls out the irony of anti-algorithm notebook content becoming algorithm fodder, while happily DIYing cheaper Field Notes-style books.
